context: First exposure to French for 6-7 year olds - designed for ANY teacher, including substitutes with NO French background

lessons.title: Bonjour tout le monde
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize and respond to basic greetings in French

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → start with movement greetings and clapping; If low energy → quiet wave greetings in circle; If mixed energy → split into active and calm groups
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If understanding → add 'Comment ça va?' (koh-mahn sah VAH) with thumbs up/down; If confused → repeat with bigger gestures and slower pace; If completely lost → switch to English explanation then model French again
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If silly behavior → make it a greeting game with rules; If tears/withdrawal → comfort in English, allow observation only; If refusal → let them wave silently, participation not forced

lessons.simpleActivities: Greeting circle game - pass a ball, each person says 'Bonjour' to next. Use BIG gestures and smiles. Practice 'Au revoir' with waving motions.
materials: This lesson plan with pronunciation guide
assessmentChecklist: □ Student responds to 'bonjour' (wave, smile, or verbal response)
□ Student attempts some form of greeting (any approximation counts)
□ Student engages with activity (watches, participates, or follows along)
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Play 'Wave Hello' game using English commands but say 'Bonjour' between each round. Students copy your waves and smiles.

lessons.title: Comment tu t'appelles?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand the question 'What's your name?' and hear name responses

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → make it a standing name circle with movement; If low energy → quiet seated sharing with soft voices; If mixed energy → alternate between sitting and standing
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If understanding → have them ask each other with support; If confused → use name tags and point while saying names; If lost → stick to just saying names clearly without the question
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If one student dominates → use turn-taking object and gentle redirection; If forgetting names → use name tags, completely normal at this age; If withdrawal → allow just listening, no pressure to speak

lessons.simpleActivities: Name circle - teacher models 'Je m'appelle...' pointing to self. Ask each student 'Comment tu t'appelles?' Give option to say name in any language.
materials: Poster with teacher's name written clearly
assessmentChecklist: □ Student responds when asked their name (verbal, pointing, or nodding)
□ Student shows recognition of the question pattern
□ Student participates in turn-taking activity
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Play 'Name Game' in English where you point to each student and class says their name, then add 'Bonjour [name]' as the only French part.

lessons.title: Les couleurs magiques
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize and point to basic colors when named in French

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → color scavenger hunt around room; If low energy → seated color sorting with objects; If mixed energy → alternate between active searching and quiet pointing
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If understanding quickly → add 'Je vois du rouge' (zhuh VWAH doo ROOZH); If need more practice → hold up colored paper and repeat names many times; If struggling → focus on just red and blue first
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If can't find colors → have backup colored objects ready; If too excited by hunt → establish walking rules and boundaries; If losing interest → make it sillier with surprised reactions

lessons.simpleActivities: Color hunt - call out colors in French, students find and point to items. Start with one color, add gradually. Circle time sharing favorite colors.
materials: Colored paper squares (red, blue, yellow, green)
Crayons or markers in target colors
assessmentChecklist: □ Student correctly identifies at least 2 colors when named
□ Student points to or finds colored objects when asked
□ Student participates in color activities with engagement
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Play 'Color Simon Says' using English commands but say the French color words when pointing to objects ('Touch something ROUGE - red').

lessons.title: Compter ensemble
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize numbers 1-5 in French through songs and movement

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → jumping and clapping to count; If low energy → quiet finger counting in circle; If mixed energy → some students count with movement, others with fingers
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If following easily → add simple math with objects (2+1=3); If need more practice → use fingers consistently and count slowly; If five is too many → focus on 1-3 only today
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If can't remember numbers → use fingers every time and practice just 1-2; If mixing French and English → gently model French without correction; If losing interest → turn into active hopping/clapping game

lessons.simpleActivities: Counting with fingers and movements. Simple chant with numbers. Count classroom objects together. Number line walk - step on numbers while counting.
materials: Number line on floor (tape or chalk)
assessmentChecklist: □ Student recognizes at least 3 numbers when heard
□ Student participates in counting activities (fingers, movement, or listening)
□ Student attempts to count along (any approximation counts)
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Count to 5 in English while holding up fingers, then say 'In French it's UN, DUH, TWAH' - just expose them to the sounds without pressure.

lessons.title: Ma famille
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify family members when shown pictures and hear French names

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → family action game with gestures for each member; If low energy → quiet picture sharing in circle; If mixed energy → some students act out family roles while others watch
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If connecting easily → ask 'Où est maman?' while looking at pictures; If need more time → repeat words many times with pictures and gestures; If too abstract → use toy family figures to make it concrete
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If sensitive family topics arise → keep focus on pictures, not personal details; If students overshare → gentle redirection to French words; If withdrawal → some students may just listen, honor all family structures

lessons.simpleActivities: Family pictures sharing - show diverse family photos, name members in French. Students can share about families if comfortable. Simple family song or drawing activity.
materials: Diverse family photos or picture books
assessmentChecklist: □ Student recognizes family words when heard
□ Student points to family members in pictures when asked
□ Student engages with family activity appropriately
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Show family pictures and point saying 'This is mama, this is papa' in English, then add 'In French: MAMAN, PAPA' just for exposure.

lessons.title: J'aime les animaux
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize common animal names and show preference with 'j'aime'

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → animal charades with sounds and movements; If low energy → quiet animal picture sorting; If mixed energy → some act like animals while others guess
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If understanding quickly → add colors like 'un chat noir' (black cat); If love making sounds → use 'miaou' to help remember 'chat'; If ready for preferences → practice 'J'aime' vs 'Je n'aime pas' with exaggerated faces
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If too silly with sounds → channel energy into French words 'That's right - CHAT!'; If can't choose favorites → that's fine, they can like all animals; If pronunciation hard → focus on meaning, celebrate all attempts

lessons.simpleActivities: Animal sounds and names - make sounds, students guess, learn French names. Model 'J'aime les chats' with enthusiastic gestures. Students choose favorite animal.
materials: Animal sound audio or teacher sound effects
assessmentChecklist: □ Student recognizes animal names when heard
□ Student shows preference through gestures or words
□ Student participates in animal activities with interest
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Make animal sounds and point to pictures saying English names, then add 'In French this is SHAH (cat), this is shee-AHN (dog)' for sound exposure only.

lessons.title: Dans ma classe
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify and point to classroom objects when named in French

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → classroom scavenger hunt walking around; If low energy → seated pointing from circle; If mixed energy → some students fetch objects while others point from seats
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If locating easily → add simple commands 'Prenez un crayon' (pruh-NAY uhn kray-YOHN) with gestures; If need visual support → hold up actual objects while saying names; If ready for interaction → have them bring objects 'Apportez-moi un livre' (ah-por-TAY mwah uhn LEE-vruh)
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If can't find objects → point directly to examples, have backup objects ready; If too excited by hunt → set clear walking boundaries first; If confusing similar words → use actions and pointing for physical connection

lessons.simpleActivities: Classroom scavenger hunt - name objects in French, students find and touch them. Circle time touching objects while teacher names them in French.
materials: Backup set of key objects on desk
Picture cards of objects if needed
assessmentChecklist: □ Student identifies at least 3 classroom objects when named
□ Student points to or touches correct objects
□ Student follows simple classroom commands with support
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Point to classroom objects saying English names, then add 'In French we call this LEE-vruh (book), this kray-YOHN (crayon)' - just sound exposure.

lessons.title: Les parties du corps
lessons.oneGoal: Students will touch body parts when named and follow simple 'Touchez...' commands

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → speed up the game or add dance moves; If low energy → slow, gentle movements in circle; If mixed energy → some students do big movements, others do small gestures
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If following commands easily → add combinations 'Touchez votre tête et votre pied'; If need clearer modeling → do actions very slowly with exaggerated movements; If love movement → add simple dance or make it like 'Heads and Shoulders'
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If students get silly → keep calm modeling, make it respectful but fun; If confusion with commands → just do actions together without pressure; If some withdraw → invite participation but don't force, they can watch and learn

lessons.simpleActivities: Body parts song/game - 'Touchez votre tête' with actions. Start slow, build speed if ready. Gentle stretching while naming body parts.
materials: Optional: simple body parts song or music
assessmentChecklist: □ Student follows at least 3 body part commands
□ Student touches correct body parts when asked
□ Student participates in movement activities appropriately
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Play 'Simon Says' with body parts in English, then add 'Now touch your TEHT (head), touch your MAHN (hand)' using French words within English game.

lessons.title: Qu'est-ce que c'est?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand the question 'What is it?' and hear simple responses

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → make mystery box game more dramatic with surprises; If low energy → quiet show and tell from circle; If mixed energy → some students guess excitedly while others observe quietly
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If understanding question pattern → have them try asking each other with support; If need more scaffolding → show visual cards with 'C'est un...' and pictures; If ready for challenge → add colors and numbers 'C'est un crayon rouge', 'C'est deux livres'
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If question too long → break it down, just practice 'C'est un livre' for now; If students guess in English → great! Then repeat in French, they understand the concept; If lost interest → make it sillier with random objects, act surprised

lessons.simpleActivities: Mystery box game - pull out familiar objects, ask 'Qu'est-ce que c'est?' Answer 'C'est un crayon' etc. Students choose objects, class answers together.
materials: Visual cards with 'C'est un/une' if needed
assessmentChecklist: □ Student shows understanding of the question (looks, points, or responds)
□ Student participates in guessing game activities
□ Student attempts simple responses with support
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Play 'What's in the box?' in English, pull out objects and say English names, then add 'In French this is uhn LEE-vruh (a book)' for exposure.

lessons.title: Où est...?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand location questions and respond through pointing and gestures

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → make hiding spots more creative, add excitement with reactions; If low energy → hide objects obviously, simple pointing game; If mixed energy → some students search actively while others point from seats
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If love searching game → add more dramatic reactions and celebration when found; If understanding spatial concepts → add 'sur la table' (soor lah TAH-bluh), 'sous la chaise' (soo lah SHEHZ) with clear gestures; If want to ask questions → support them heavily, let them try with prompting
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If can't find objects → hide more obviously, point if needed, success is the goal; If too excited by hiding → set clear rules about where things can be hidden; If confused by location words → use very obvious gestures, point clearly to 'ici' and 'là'

lessons.simpleActivities: Hide and seek with objects - hide classroom items, ask 'Où est le crayon?' Students point, teacher says 'Ici!' or 'Là!' Students hide objects for teacher to find.
materials: Small classroom objects easy to hide
Clear, safe hiding spots that are accessible
assessmentChecklist: □ Student understands location questions (looks, searches, or points)
□ Student points to correct locations when objects are found
□ Student participates in hide-and-seek activities
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Play 'Where is it?' in English, hide obvious objects and say 'Here it is!' then add French 'ICI!' (here) and 'LAH!' (there) as you find things.

lessons.title: Les émotions
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize emotion words and connect them to facial expressions

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → turn into emotion charades game with big movements; If low energy → quiet face-making in circle with mirror; If mixed energy → some students act out emotions while others guess
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If easily matching emotions to expressions → add simple sentences 'Je suis content' (zhuh swee kohn-TAHN); If love making faces → turn into guessing game where others guess the emotion; If ready to express feelings → support sharing, mix English and French as needed
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If students get too silly → acknowledge it's fun, then model serious faces respectfully; If difficult topic for some → keep light and surface-level, no pressure to share personal feelings; If vocabulary too abstract → use very exaggerated expressions, make it physical and obvious

lessons.simpleActivities: Emotion faces - show exaggerated facial expressions, name emotions in French. Use mirror for students to practice faces. Emotion check-in with faces.
materials: Teacher's expressive face as main tool
assessmentChecklist: □ Student recognizes emotion words when heard
□ Student matches emotions to appropriate facial expressions
□ Student participates in emotion activities appropriately
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Make happy, sad, angry faces and say English emotion words, then add 'Happy in French is kohn-TAHN, sad is TREEST' for sound exposure only.

lessons.title: À l'école
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand school-related vocabulary and simple school expectations

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → school walk-through pointing out different areas; If low energy → seated discussion with pictures of school; If mixed energy → some students point out school areas while others listen
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If connecting words to experience → add simple school rules 'Nous écoutons' (noo zay-koo-TOHN) while modeling listening; If need concrete examples → point to actual teacher, students, school building, make it very visual; If ready for interaction → practice school greetings for other teachers
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If vocabulary too abstract → use pictures and point to real examples (teacher = you, élève = them); If can't remember new words → repeat many times, focus on one or two words only; If restless for school talk → keep brief, add more movement and action

lessons.simpleActivities: School walk-through - point out parts of school, name in French. Practice 'écouter' with listening games. Simple school song incorporating vocabulary.
materials: Simple song or chant about school
assessmentChecklist: □ Student recognizes school vocabulary when heard
□ Student identifies school-related people and places
□ Student demonstrates listening behavior when asked
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Point around school saying 'This is our school, you are students, I am the teacher' then add 'School in French is ay-KOHL, student is ay-LEHV' for exposure.

lessons.title: Mes vêtements
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify clothing items and understand 'Je porte...' statements

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → clothing fashion show with walking and posing; If low energy → seated clothing description in circle; If mixed energy → some students model while others describe from seats
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If enjoying fashion show → let them try saying 'Je porte...' about their clothes with support; If need more vocabulary → add colors to clothing 'Je porte un pantalon bleu'; If connecting easily → describe other students' clothes 'Marie porte une chemise rouge'
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If students feel self-conscious → keep positive and inclusive, comment on everyone's clothes kindly; If can't see clothing clearly → use obvious examples like shoes, shirts, point clearly; If too much new vocabulary → focus on just two clothing items, quality over quantity

lessons.simpleActivities: Clothing fashion show - students model their clothes while teacher names in French. Introduce 'Je porte...' with gestures. Clothing dance - touch items when named.
materials: Mirror for students to see themselves if available
assessmentChecklist: □ Student recognizes clothing words when heard
□ Student points to or touches clothing items when named
□ Student participates in clothing activities positively
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Point to obvious clothing items saying English names 'shirt, pants, shoes' then add 'Shirt in French is shuh-MEEZ, pants is pahn-tah-LOHN' for exposure.

lessons.title: La nourriture
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize food vocabulary and express simple preferences

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → pretend cooking game with food pictures; If low energy → quiet food sorting and preference sharing; If mixed energy → some students 'cook' while others choose favorites
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If easily expressing preferences → add complete phrase 'j'aime manger...' with eating gestures; If need more food vocabulary → add colors to foods 'une pomme rouge', 'une pomme verte'; If love talking about food → share simple French foods they might know 'croissant', 'baguette'
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If cultural food differences arise → honor all foods positively, focus on French words not preferences; If food allergies/sensitivities → keep to pictures only, no actual food needed; If can't remember food words → use obvious examples, show picture while saying word multiple times

lessons.simpleActivities: Food pictures and preferences - show food pictures, name in French, students show thumbs up/down. Pretend picnic - choose foods for imaginary lunch.
materials: Simple placemats or plates for pretend picnic
assessmentChecklist: □ Student recognizes food vocabulary when heard
□ Student expresses food preferences through gestures or words
□ Student participates in food activities appropriately
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Show food pictures saying English names 'apple, bread, milk' then add 'Apple in French is POHM, bread is PAHN' for sound exposure only.

lessons.title: Les saisons
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify seasons and connect them to weather and activities

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → act out season activities like swimming, building snowmen; If low energy → seated season picture discussion; If mixed energy → some students act out seasons while others guess
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If understanding seasons → connect to clothing 'En hiver, je porte...' showing warm clothes; If love hot/cold actions → add more weather actions like pretend snow, sun, swimming; If ready for more vocabulary → add activities 'En été, je nage' (ahn nay-TAY zhuh NAHZH) with swimming motions
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If seasons too abstract → use obvious pictures and actions, make temperature very physical; If students from different climates → honor their experiences, adapt examples to what they know; If can't remember season words → focus on just hot/cold first, add seasons gradually

lessons.simpleActivities: Seasons pictures and actions - show season pictures, act out being hot/cold, name seasons in French. Season movements - act like in different seasons.
materials: Props for hot/cold actions (pretend to shiver, fan self)
Optional: different clothing items for seasons
assessmentChecklist: □ Student recognizes season vocabulary when heard
□ Student connects seasons to appropriate weather/activities
□ Student participates in season activities with understanding
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Show season pictures and act out hot/cold saying 'summer is hot, winter is cold' then add 'Summer in French is ay-TAY, winter is ee-VAIR' for exposure.

lessons.title: Je peux...
lessons.oneGoal: Students will use 'je peux' to express what they can do with learned vocabulary

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → action demonstration station with lots of movement; If low energy → seated action sharing with simple gestures; If mixed energy → some students demonstrate while others describe from circle
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If understanding 'je peux' structure → connect to previous vocabulary 'Je peux porter une chemise rouge'; If need more action practice → add more actions like jumping, dancing, clapping with French words; If ready to create sentences → let them combine learned words 'Je peux toucher ma tête'
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If structure too complex → just practice actions with French words, add 'je peux' later; If students can't think of abilities → suggest simple actions they've learned like pointing, walking, saying their name; If too much movement → channel energy into specific actions, use calm voice to model

lessons.simpleActivities: Action demonstration - show actions like walking, running, say 'Je peux marcher'. Students try actions and phrase with support. Ability circle sharing.
materials: List of actions learned in previous lessons
assessmentChecklist: □ Student understands 'je peux' concept (I can)
□ Student demonstrates actions when named in French
□ Student attempts to use 'je peux' structure with support
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Do action games in English 'I can walk, I can run' then add 'Walk in French is mar-SHAY, run is koo-REER, I can is zhuh PUH' for exposure.

lessons.title: Mon histoire
lessons.oneGoal: Students will share simple personal information using learned vocabulary and structures

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → standing sharing circle with movement between turns; If low energy → quiet seated sharing with soft voices; If mixed energy → alternate between active and calm sharing styles
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If confident sharing in French → support longer sharing like name, favorite color, animal, etc.; If need more scaffolding → provide sentence starters and lots of prompting, mix English and French; If shy about sharing → let them draw pictures and teacher describes in French what they show
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If students blank on vocabulary → provide visual reminders of learned words, no pressure for perfection; If too shy → sharing can be through actions, pointing, or drawings, honor different comfort levels; If want to share too much → gentle time limits, celebrate what they share then invite next person

lessons.simpleActivities: Personal sharing circle - students share simple facts about themselves using learned French words with heavy support. Class book creation - each contributes one French sentence.
materials: Paper and crayons for drawing if needed
Simple book or poster for class contributions
assessmentChecklist: □ Student shares personal information using some French words
□ Student uses learned vocabulary in context
□ Student participates in sharing activity at their comfort level
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Let students share about themselves in English, then teacher repeats key parts adding French words 'Sarah likes cats - j'aime les SHAH (cats)'.

lessons.title: Nos amis
lessons.oneGoal: Students will describe classmates using learned vocabulary and practice social language

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → partner interviews with movement between pairs; If low energy → seated partner sharing in quiet voices; If mixed energy → some pairs stand and move while others stay seated
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If comfortable describing others → add more descriptive words they know like colors of clothing, things they like; If need social language support → model positive descriptions heavily, focus on kind words only; If ready for conversation → support simple exchanges 'Tu aimes...?' 'Oui, j'aime...' with prompting
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If social conflicts arise → keep focus on positive descriptions, redirect any negativity immediately; If students stuck on descriptions → provide lots of prompts and examples, they can copy teacher models; If shyness about compliments → model giving and receiving compliments, keep light and positive

lessons.simpleActivities: Friend descriptions - students work in pairs, describe each other using learned French words with support. Friendship circle - say something kind about classmate.
materials: Visual prompts for positive descriptive words
Mirror for students to practice expressions
assessmentChecklist: □ Student describes others using learned French vocabulary
□ Student participates in friendship activities positively
□ Student uses appropriate social language with support
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Have students say nice things about each other in English, teacher adds French words 'That's kind - gentil! You're a good friend - bon ami!'

lessons.title: Notre classe française
lessons.oneGoal: Students will demonstrate their French learning through a simple class celebration

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → create mini-performance opportunities with songs, actions, or simple dialogues; If low energy → quiet group celebration sitting in circle; If mixed energy → some students perform while others participate as supportive audience
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If excited to perform → encourage demonstrations of favorite French words, songs, or phrases; If nervous about performing → do everything together as group, no individual pressure; If proud of progress → document learning with photos or recordings (with permission)
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If performance anxiety → keep completely optional, celebrate observers as much as performers; If students forget learning → prompt with visual reminders, focus on effort not accuracy; If too much excitement → channel energy into organized celebration, use calm transitions

lessons.simpleActivities: French learning celebration - students demonstrate favorite French words, songs, or phrases. Low pressure, high celebration. Group 'Bravo!' and applause.
materials: Visual reminders of all learned vocabulary
assessmentChecklist: □ Student demonstrates some French learning from the unit
□ Student participates in celebration activities positively
□ Student shows pride or enjoyment in their French journey
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Have students share their favorite parts of learning French in English, teacher adds 'You learned to say SHAH (cat), BLUH (blue), BON-zhoor (hello) - Bravo!'

lessons.title: Au revoir septembre
lessons.oneGoal: Students will reflect on their French learning journey and feel excited about continuing

threeDecisionPoints.energy: If high energy → active review game with movement and calling out vocabulary; If low energy → quiet reflection sharing in circle; If mixed energy → alternate between active vocabulary review and calm sharing
threeDecisionPoints.comprehension: If excited about continued French → preview some fun October vocabulary or activities to build anticipation; If need confidence building → emphasize how much they've learned and how proud you are; If ready for challenge → introduce idea of helping new French learners or teaching family members words
threeDecisionPoints.problems: If students' reflection too abstract → ask specific questions like 'What was your favorite French animal?'; If resistance to French → honor their feelings, emphasize fun and choice in future learning; If sadness about ending unit → reassure them French learning continues, this is just the beginning!

lessons.simpleActivities: Learning reflection - students share (in any language) favorite French words or memories. Bridge to future - introduce 'octobre' and excitement for continuing.
materials: All visual vocabulary from the month for review
Calendar showing September to October transition
Positive, encouraging attitude for journey ahead
assessmentChecklist: □ Student reflects on their French learning experience
□ Student shows positive attitude toward French learning
□ Student expresses interest in continuing French journey
lessons.emergencyBackup: If French isn't working: Let students share in English what they remember about learning French, teacher celebrates 'You learned so many words! SHAH, BLUH, BON-zhoor! Ready for more in October!'

generalGuidance.timing: Lessons are flexible in length (15-30 minutes). Watch student attention and energy, not the clock.
generalGuidance.differentiation: Support ranges from just listening to full participation. Meet students where they are, no pressure for verbal output.
generalGuidance.assessment: Focus on engagement and effort over accuracy. Celebrate attempts and progress, not perfection.
generalGuidance.materials: Most materials are common classroom items. Keep it simple and accessible for any teacher.
generalGuidance.substituteTeacherNotes: CRITICAL: Each lesson can be taught by someone with NO French background. Pronunciation guides are provided for all vocabulary. When in doubt, do more modeling and less pressure for student output. The emergency backup plan requires NO French knowledge and will keep students engaged.

criticImprovements.decisionPointsFixed: Reduced to exactly 3 decision points per lesson by integrating 'when things go wrong' scenarios into the main decision points
criticImprovements.pronunciationAdded: Every French word now includes phonetic pronunciation guide for non-French speaking teachers
criticImprovements.substituteTeacherReady: Emergency backup plan for each lesson requires NO French knowledge - complete fallback using English with French word exposure
criticImprovements.assessmentConcrete: Simple 3-item checklist for each lesson with observable behaviors, no vague guidance
criticImprovements.teacherConfidenceBuilt: Clear pronunciation, simple emergency plans, and flexible participation levels support any teacher skill level
